title: Plain-language incident recap and self-triage kit
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a customer-facing, plain-language recap and an actionable self-triage kit that customer-success can post to the status page and send to impacted customers. It’s intentionally concise, avoids internal jargon, and gives clear next steps customers can take while we finish the technical postmortem.

Summary (TL;DR):
On 2029-11-05 between ~09:22–10:18 UTC we experienced elevated error rates and delayed responses for inference requests served from the us-west-2 region for a subset of tenants. Impact: up to 6% of requests returned 5xx or timed out for ~55 minutes; streaming sessions for long responses were most affected. Root-cause (high level): an unexpected interaction between autoscaling decisions and a cache eviction race that caused request routing to fall back to slower model variants and intermittently exceed connection timeouts.

Customer-facing timeline (short):
- 09:22 UTC: First customer reports and internal alerts triggered.
- 09:25 UTC: We started rolling temporary routing rules to avoid the affected autoscaler path.
- 09:37 UTC: Temporary routing reduced error rate by ~40% for tested tenants.
- 09:55 UTC: We applied a configuration lock to prevent further concurrent autoscaler decisions.
- 10:12 UTC: Full recovery observed in us-west-2; monitoring shows normal error rates and latency.

What we did for customers immediately: (actions you can rely on)
- Rolled temporary routing to keep production traffic on stable model variants until a safe autoscaler fix is deployed.
- Applied a configuration lock to stop the autoscaler from making concurrent risky decisions.
- Scoped the fix to avoid replaying requests or changing model outputs for processed requests — no customer data was reprocessed.

Customer self-triage checklist (what to check on your side now):
1) Confirm you aren’t seeing 5xx errors or timeouts in your app logs (look for status 502/504 or connection timeouts)
2) If you use streaming, verify partial responses are being resumed or completed (check session IDs / stream tokens)
3) If you run long-running batch jobs, check for queued requests that may have been retried — do not re-run jobs until you confirm with us if you saw many retries
4) If you have automated alerting tied to our latency thresholds, consider temporarily suppressing alerts for the 09:00–11:00 UTC window while you reconcile logs

Data integrity and customer data concerns:
- No input data was dropped from our persistent storage; however some in-flight requests returned errors and were not processed. We did not reprocess failed requests automatically.
- If you need assistance reconciling request IDs from 09:22–10:18 UTC, provide a short list of sample request IDs or timestamp ranges and we will prioritize a replay/validation package.

Short-term mitigations we’ve deployed (what we changed immediately):
- Prevented the autoscaler from taking concurrent scale-down+scale-up decisions for 30 minutes after a heuristic threshold breach.
- Added a conservative cache-eviction delay to avoid the race between KV cache invalidation and routing decisions.
- Deployed extra capacity in us-west-2 for the affected model families and enabled graceful fallback to warm replicas.

Expected next steps (customer-facing schedule):
- 24–48 hours: We’ll publish an internal postmortem (technical) and a customer summary with an itemized rollback/fix timeline.
- 3–7 days: Patch to autoscaler decision logic and a configuration option you can opt into to prioritize latency vs cost during autoscaler transients.
- 14 days: Follow-up release with telemetry hooks exposed to tenants for earlier detection of similar cache-routing interactions.

If you need immediate help (how to reach us):
- For high-severity impact (production outage or data integrity concern) open a Priority-1 support case: support+priority@redwood.ai or call your account team number.
- For assistance reconciling request IDs or replay packages: reply to this message with up to 10 sample request IDs and time ranges and we’ll queue a focused analysis.

Suggested statuspage blurb (short, plain language you can paste):
"We experienced increased errors and latency for some inference requests in us-west-2 from ~09:22–10:18 UTC on 2029-11-05. The issue was caused by an interaction between autoscaling and cache eviction that increased routing to slower model variants. We applied temporary routing protections and capacity increases; normal service resumed at ~10:12 UTC. No customer data was lost. Full technical postmortem and replay guidance will be published within 48 hours."

Suggested FAQ (ready-to-send answers):
Q: Were any customer inputs lost?
A: No stored inputs were lost. Some in-flight requests returned errors and were not processed; we did not re-run those automatically. If you saw failed requests, we can help validate and, where appropriate, replay them on request.

Q: Do I need to change my integration?
A: Not immediately. We’ve applied routing and autoscaler safeguards. If you require stricter latency guarantees during future autoscaling events, you can opt into the forthcoming "stable-routing" tenant config that we expect to release in the next week.

Q: Will I be refunded or receive credits?
A: We evaluate credits on a case-by-case basis based on SLA impact and customer usage. If you believe you qualify, open a support request with your tenant ID and sample impacted request IDs and our customer-success team will review.

Internal notes for CS reps (short):
- Do not promise a technical timeline beyond the 48-hour customer summary.
- Offer replay assistance for small sets of request IDs; escalate larger reconciliation requests to Solutions Eng (eng-solutions@redwood.ai) with Jira INC-6789 tag.
- Use conservative language: emphasize mitigations applied, no data loss in storage, offer replay help.

Appendix: quick checklist for generating a customer replay package (internal use)
- Confirm tenant ID and provide up to 10 example request IDs + UTC timestamps.
- Gather logs from our edge gateways + model routing logs for the requested times.
- Run a controlled replay to a warm replica with identical model variant and report differences.

Document history:
- 2029-11-05: initial note (Lena Chen)
- 2029-11-06: added short timeline and mitigations (Aisha Patel)
- 2029-11-07: review updates and statuspage blurb (Miguel Torres)

Notes / Open questions for follow-up:
- Confirm whether any customers saw duplicate responses from retry logic; we need to know if any clients automatically retried idempotent vs non-idempotent requests.
- Decide if the "stable-routing" tenant option will be on by default or opt-in.

End of doc.
